vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: create-harness-docs
Version: 1.0.0

The skill bundle is a project scaffolding and documentation tool designed to implement 'Harness Engineering' standards. It analyzes the local project structure (detecting languages, frameworks, and business domains) and generates Markdown documentation, a GitHub Actions CI workflow, and an architecture linting script (scripts/create-harness-docs.js). While it uses potentially sensitive operations like file system writes and a hardcoded shell command (find/wc) for file counting, these actions are strictly aligned with its stated purpose and show no signs of malicious intent or data exfiltration.

llm.summary: The skill is internally consistent: it scans a repository and writes documentation, CI config, and helper scripts — nothing in the package requires unrelated credentials or network access, but you should review generated CI/workflow and scripts before committing.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (generate Harness-style docs) match the actual artifacts and operations: the script scans the repo, creates docs (AGENTS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, domain pages, quality grades), creates directories, and writes a GitHub Actions workflow and check script. All required actions are proportionate to the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the script limit themselves to scanning the project tree and writing documentation/CI/check scripts. However, the skill will create .github/workflows/harness-ci.yml and scripts/check-layers.js (or similar) in the repo — generated CI can run on push, so review those files before pushing. The AGENTS.md text discouraging hand-written code and encouraging Agent-generated code is a policy preference in the docs (not behavior in the script), but it's notable guidance that could affect workflows if followed.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec; the skill is instruction-plus-source only. The included Node script writes files locally and invokes local shell commands (find) via execSync. The sources come bundled (no external downloads or package installs).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables, no credentials, and references only local filesystem paths under the project root. There are no requests for unrelated secrets or external service tokens.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not modify other skills or global agent configs. It does write repository files (including a GitHub Actions workflow), which persist in the repo and could trigger CI on push — review those generated files before committing or pushing to avoid unintended automation.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: scan the repo and create Harness-style documentation, CI workflow, and helper scripts. Before running it in a real project: 1) run it in a disposable branch or copy of the repo so you can review all generated files; 2) inspect the created .github/workflows/harness-ci.yml and any scripts (e.g., check-layers.js) to ensure they don't run unexpected commands or contact external services; 3) note that the script uses execSync to run local shell commands (e.g., find), so run it on a trusted machine; 4) if you plan to follow the AGENTS.md guidance about automated Agents generating and merging code, consider the security implications of enabling such automation and lock down repository secrets and CI permissions accordingly. Minor nit: the check script shebang in the bundled code appears to use 'nod' instead of 'node' which looks like a typo — expect a small bug there to fix before relying on the check script.
